It is static analysis for Python repositories. It never calls a model, uploads code or runs your program, except the validation command you give it, and only in a throwaway copy.

items.s: Compares the commit before the agent’s work with everything after it: committed, staged, unstaged and untracked.
Builds the import graph from real roots: entry points, framework apps, Dockerfile, Compose or Procfile commands, packaging entry points.
For an old file, finds the new one that took over: AST, symbol and token similarity, moved call sites, public names kept.
Only a stale file with a replacement, confidence ≥ 0.85 and risk ≤ 0.20 is proposed. eval, dynamic imports, parse errors or templated deploy commands switch deletion off for the whole repository.
Deleting needs the exact JSON plan a person reviewed, a validation command that passes in an isolated copy, and hashes that still match. A snapshot allows a restore.

items.s: Opening a task records the intent, acceptance criteria, constraints and non-goals. It starts as a draft with no write authority.
Context routing seals what may be written, what is read-only and what is forbidden. Reading may grow later; write authority never does.
PSG reads the final change set from Git itself, not from the agent, and checks it against the boundary, locks and policies.
Only checks named in the project config run. Results are runtime-attested and tied to the worktree, so any later edit makes them stale.
A finding blocks only if the patch caused it, it breaks an acceptance criterion or a constraint, and the evidence holds. Then the gate says SHIPPABLE and review stops.

Some shapes are carried almost only by colour: a number drawn in one colour among others, a pattern that survives in hue while brightness stays flat. People with colour-vision differences, OCR and general vision models can all miss it, or worse, confidently read something that is not there.

Tools that “enhance” such images usually return a single picture or a single answer. ChromaRecover returns the spatial structure itself, the evidence that supports it, and an explicit status: ok, uncertain or retry recommended. When the evidence is weak, it says so instead of guessing.
